newsitem.title: UK: GDR REPORT-GDRs neutral after India rail budget.
newsitem.headline: GDR REPORT-GDRs neutral after India rail budget.

text.p: Indian global depositary receipts (GDRs) dipped on the announcement of the 1997-98 railway budget on Wednesday but then recovered to end the day on neutral ground, dealers said.
"GDRs traded down earlier, they then steadied up a little bit -- they recovered the ground they lost in the morning but they didn't end up on the day," said one trader at a brokerage here.
Railway Minister Ram Vilas Paswan announced plans to raise rail freight rates by 12 percent for all commodities barring essentials and for all distances during Wednesday's session.
The trader said that level had come in the middle of expectations that had ranged from 11 to 14 percent. Shares on the underlying markets shrugged off the budget news.
The HSBC James Capel Indian GDR index JCEAI rose 1.03 percent, or 0.68 points, to 66.73 during the session, with the premium over the local market at 14.85 percent.
The Cazenove Indian GDR Index firmed 0.55 percent, or 0.41 points, to 74.68 after the Bombay Stock Exchange 30 share index rose almost 10 points to 3,366.50.
One trader said the bulk producers, cement, steel and paper stocks had eased in Bombay early in the session.
"We're seeing client sellers, people are lining up to go neutral into Friday's budget," he said.
Most traders are expecting little activity ahead of Friday's main budget announcement, due after the local market closes around midday London time. GDRs will continue to trade in London.

Taiwanese GDRs slipped 2.15 percent to 66.73 on the Capel Taiwan GDR Index after heavy profit-taking on electronics stocks sent prices south on the local share market. The premium over local shares was 1.47 percent.
The Capel Korea GDR Index meanwhile lost 0.66 percent to 59.56, with a 34.16 percent premium over the local market.
